title: Cluster Architecture and Extension Interfaces

header.html: Understand extension interfaces (CNI, CSI, CRI, etc.); this module also gives the map you need for every troubleshooting task
Kubernetes v1.37.0 (kubeadm-style layout in kind nodes)

toc.title: How a Pod gets created (the story)

html:
1The map of a cluster

A cluster has a control plane (the decision makers) and worker nodes (where Pods run). In a kubeadm-style cluster the control plane runs as static Pods on the control plane node.

Component Where it runs Job
kube-apiserver control plane, static Pod The front door. Every kubectl call, every kubelet and controller talks to it. Only it talks to etcd.
etcd control plane, static Pod The database of all cluster state.
kube-scheduler control plane, static Pod Picks a node for each new Pod.
kube-controller-manager control plane, static Pod Runs the controllers (Deployment, ReplicaSet, Node, Namespace, ...) that move actual state toward desired state.
kubelet every node, a systemd service (not a Pod) Starts the containers of Pods assigned to its node and reports status.
kube-proxy every node, DaemonSet Programs Service rules on the node.
Container runtime every node Runs containers (here containerd).
CoreDNS Deployment in kube-system Cluster DNS.

Exam fact to remember: the kubelet is a service on the node. If it stops, the node goes NotReady. The other control plane parts are Pods, so you read their logs with kubectl logs or, when the API server is down, with crictl.

2Static Pods

A static Pod is defined by a file on a node, not by the API server. The kubelet watches a directory and runs whatever manifest it finds there. The API server shows a read-only mirror Pod whose name ends with the node name (etcd-cka-control-plane).

  • Directory: set by staticPodPath in the kubelet config file /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml. On kubeadm clusters it is /etc/kubernetes/manifests.
  • Create one: write a Pod manifest into that directory on that node. Remove it by deleting the file. kubectl delete pod only removes the mirror, and the kubelet recreates it.
  • Edit a control plane component (for example an API server flag) by editing its manifest. The kubelet restarts it by itself.
ssh cka-worker
grep staticPodPath /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml     # find the directory
cat > /etc/kubernetes/manifests/static-web.yaml <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: static-web
spec:
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
Y

The mirror Pod appears as static-web-<node name>; its owner reference kind is Node.

3Where things live (kubeadm layout)

What Path
Static Pod manifests /etc/kubernetes/manifests/
Certificates /etc/kubernetes/pki/ (etcd's in /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/)
Admin kubeconfig /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
Kubelet configuration /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml
CNI configuration /etc/cni/net.d/
Service ClusterIP range --service-cluster-ip-range flag in kube-apiserver.yaml

Find an API server flag fast:

grep service-cluster-ip-range /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml

4Container runtime and crictl

The kubelet talks to the runtime through the Container Runtime Interface (CRI). Here the runtime is containerd. crictl is the node-level tool that speaks CRI, and it is your tool when kubectl does not work.

Task Command (on the node)
List running containers crictl ps (add -a for stopped ones)
Filter by name crictl ps --name kube-proxy
IDs only crictl ps --name kube-proxy -q
Logs of a container crictl logs <id>
List Pod sandboxes crictl pods

5Extension interfaces: CNI, CSI, CRI

Kubernetes does not ship networking, storage or a runtime. It defines interfaces and plugins implement them.

Interface Full name What plugs in How you see it
CRI Container Runtime Interface the runtime (containerd, CRI-O) kubectl get nodes -o wide (CONTAINER-RUNTIME column)
CNI Container Network Interface the Pod network (kindnet, Calico, Cilium, ...) config file in /etc/cni/net.d/ on the node
CSI Container Storage Interface storage drivers kubectl get csidrivers, kubectl get storageclass
  • No CNI plugin means Pods stay ContainerCreating and nodes are NotReady.
  • In the lab cluster the CNI is kindnet; its file is /etc/cni/net.d/10-kindnet.conflist.
  • A RuntimeClass chooses a runtime handler for a Pod:
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata: {name: standard}
handler: runc            # must match a runtime configured in containerd
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: rtc}
spec:
  runtimeClassName: standard
  containers: [{name: web, image: nginx:alpine}]

If the handler does not exist in containerd, the Pod never starts (see Lab 1.5's wrong answer).

6How a Pod gets created (the story)

  1. kubectl sends the request to the API server, which authenticates, authorizes, validates and writes it to etcd.
  2. The Deployment controller (in the controller manager) creates a ReplicaSet, which creates Pods.
  3. The scheduler sees Pods with no node and writes a node name.
  4. The kubelet on that node sees its Pod, asks the runtime (CRI) to start containers and the CNI plugin to wire the network.
  5. kube-proxy keeps Service rules current on every node.

Exam use: when a Pod is stuck, find which step stopped. Pending with no node = scheduler. ContainerCreating for long = CNI, image pull or volume. NotReady node = kubelet.

7Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m01 -->

Lab 1.1: service cidr

Domain: Architecture | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-01-service-cidr)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Find the IP range from which Service ClusterIPs are allocated in this cluster and write it (for example 10.0.0.0/8) to ~/answers/svc-cidr.txt. Hint: it is a flag of one control plane component.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'grep service-cluster-ip-range /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane "grep -o 'service-cluster-ip-range=[0-9./]*' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml | cut -d= -f2" > ~/answers/svc-cidr.txt

Lab 1.2: static pod

Domain: Architecture | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-02-static-pod)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create a static Pod named static-web with image nginx:alpine on the node cka-worker. Find the directory the kubelet watches for static Pod manifests from the kubelet configuration file. The Pod must run in the default namespace.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker 'grep staticPodPath /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml'
ssh cka-worker 'mkdir -p /etc/kubernetes/manifests && cat > /etc/kubernetes/manifests/static-web.yaml <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: static-web
spec:
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
Y'
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/static-web-cka-worker --timeout=120s

Lab 1.3: crictl container

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-03-crictl-container)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

On the node cka-worker, use crictl to find the ID of the running container named kube-proxy and write the full container ID to ~/answers/cid.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker 'crictl ps --name kube-proxy -q' > ~/answers/cid.txt
cat ~/answers/cid.txt

Lab 1.4: cni config

Domain: Architecture | Points: 3 | Time: about 3 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-04-cni-config)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Pod networking on node cka-worker is set up by a CNI plugin. Find the name of the CNI configuration file in the directory the kubelet runtime reads (/etc/cni/net.d) on that node and write only the file name to ~/answers/cni.txt.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-worker 'ls /etc/cni/net.d' > ~/answers/cni.txt

Lab 1.5: runtimeclass

Domain: Workloads | Points: 5 | Time: about 5 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-05-runtimeclass)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Create a RuntimeClass named standard that uses the container runtime handler runc. Then create a Pod named rtc in the namespace rt with image nginx:alpine that uses this RuntimeClass.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: node.k8s.io/v1
kind: RuntimeClass
metadata:
  name: standard
handler: runc
Y
kubectl -n rt apply -f - <<Y
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: rtc
spec:
  runtimeClassName: standard
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:alpine
Y
kubectl -n rt wait --for=condition=Ready pod/rtc --timeout=120s

Lab 1.6: node versions

Domain: Architecture | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-06-node-versions)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Write one line per node to ~/answers/versions.txt on the host, in the form <node name> <kubelet version> (for example node1 v1.37.0), sorted by node name, using JSONPath or custom columns (no header line).

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}{"\n"}{end}' | sort > ~/answers/versions.txt
cat ~/answers/versions.txt

Lab 1.7: etcd image

Domain: Architecture | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m01-07-etcd-image)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

Find the container image (name and tag) that the etcd static Pod uses, by reading the manifest on the control plane node (not by asking the API server), and write only the image to ~/answers/etcd-image.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

ssh cka-control-plane 'grep "image:" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml'
ssh cka-control-plane "grep 'image:' /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml | awk '{print \$2}'" > ~/answers/etcd-image.txt

<!-- /LABS -->

8Recall questions

R1Which component is the only one that talks to etcd?

Show the answer

The API server.

R2How does the kubelet run on a kubeadm cluster node?

Show the answer

As a systemd service, not as a Pod.

R3Where do static Pod manifests live, and how do you find the exact path?

Show the answer

Usually /etc/kubernetes/manifests; the staticPodPath field in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml gives the path.

R4You run kubectl delete pod on a static Pod. What happens?

Show the answer

Only the mirror Pod is removed; the kubelet recreates it. Delete the manifest file to remove the Pod.

R5Which tool inspects containers on a node when the API server is down?

Show the answer

crictl.

R6What do CNI, CSI and CRI each plug in?

Show the answer

CNI the Pod network, CSI storage drivers, CRI the container runtime.

R7A new node stays NotReady and Pods stay ContainerCreating. Which extension is the first suspect?

Show the answer

The CNI plugin (its configuration in /etc/cni/net.d/).

R8Where is the Service ClusterIP range configured?

Show the answer

The --service-cluster-ip-range flag of the API server (its static Pod manifest).

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Control plane apiserver, etcd, scheduler, controller-manager as static Pods
Node kubelet (systemd), kube-proxy (DaemonSet), runtime
Static Pod dir staticPodPath in /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml, usually /etc/kubernetes/manifests
Certificates /etc/kubernetes/pki/
CNI config /etc/cni/net.d/
Node-level container tool crictl ps, crictl logs
Interfaces CRI runtime, CNI network, CSI storage
